definitions.explanation: Having value or purpose; worth spending time or effort on. Used to describe experiences, time, discussions, and activities that produce something positive.

examples.japanese: {有意義|ゆういぎ}な{時間|じかん}を{過|す}ごした。
とても{有意義|ゆういぎ}な{議論|ぎろん}ができた。
examples.english: We were able to have a very worthwhile discussion.

examples.japanese: {休日|きゅうじつ}を{有意義|ゆういぎ}に{使|つか}うために{読書|どくしょ}をしている。
examples.english: I'm reading to make good use of my day off.

notes:
{有意義|ゆういぎ} is a na-adjective meaning something has real value or purpose — worth the time and effort invested.

FORMS:
- Na-adjective: {有意義|ゆういぎ}な{時間|じかん} (meaningful time)
- Adverbial: {有意義|ゆういぎ}に{過|す}ごす (to spend meaningfully)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {有意義|ゆういぎ}な{時間|じかん} (meaningful time)
- {有意義|ゆういぎ}な{経験|けいけん} (worthwhile experience)
- {有意義|ゆういぎ}な{議論|ぎろん} (meaningful discussion)
- {有意義|ゆういぎ}な{活動|かつどう} (worthwhile activity)
- {有意義|ゆういぎ}に{使|つか}う (to put to good use)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {無意味|むいみ}: meaningless, pointless (closer antonym in everyday use)
- {無駄|むだ}: wasteful, useless (focuses on wasted effort)

REGISTER:
Slightly formal. Often used in speeches, evaluations, and reflections. Very common after events or experiences: とても{有意義|ゆういぎ}な{一日|いちにち}でした (It was a very meaningful day).
